paras: The Enigma shooting into Black shanties was a night attack on 11 June 1903 at Enigma, Georgia, in which unknown parties fired into the homes of Black residents of the town's still quarter. No one was killed, and warrants were said to have been issued for some of the leaders. The episode is known from a single paragraph in a Tifton correspondence column of the Savannah Morning News.

According to the Tifton correspondent, the trouble "between whites and blacks" at Enigma grew out of a fight between a Black boy and a white boy. The quarrel was then "taken up later by older heads that should have been cooler," in the correspondent's words.

Late that night unknown parties came to the still quarter and fired into the "negro shanties." The shots killed no one, and the column reported no injuries, though it said the residents were "pretty badly frightened." The report did not name the shooters, give their number, or state their race.
The column stated that "it is said" warrants had been issued for some of the leaders, without naming them. No later report of arrests, a hearing or a trial appears in the coverage.

The Savannah Morning News ran the item on 13 June 1903 in its "Topics of Tifton" column, dated Tifton, June 12, placing it between news of a railroad sale and a report of burglaries in Tifton. The correspondent faulted the adults who had escalated the boys' fight and called it fortunate that no one was killed, while referring to the residents as "darkies." No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the shooting.

accounts.label: Tifton correspondent
accounts.gist: A fight between a Black boy and a white boy at Enigma was taken up by adults; that night unknown parties fired into the Black shanties in the still quarter, killing no one, and warrants were said to have been issued for some leaders.

framing.detail: The Tifton column faults 'older heads that should have been cooler' and calls it fortunate no one was killed, but refers to the residents as 'darkies' and gives the episode one paragraph between business and burglary news.

record_check.dossier: The article names only Enigma and a Tifton dateline; it gives no county.
Shooting into occupied dwellings (the 'negro shanties'), not at named persons.
Add that warrants were 'said' to have been issued for some of the leaders.
No injuries reported; the paper says only that no one was killed and residents were frightened, so injuries are unreported rather than confirmed zero.

info: The trouble arose 'yesterday' relative to a Tifton dispatch dated June 12, i.e. 11 June 1903; the shooting was 'late at night', apparently the same night
None; the trouble grew out of a fight between a Black boy and a white boy that adults 'took up'
'Unknown parties'; the paper does not state their race

sources.note: 'Topics of Tifton' column, dated Tifton June 12: a fight between a Black boy and a white boy at Enigma, taken up by adults, ended with unknown parties firing into Black shanties in the still quarter at night; no one killed; warrants said to be issued.
quotes: Some trouble arose at Enigma yesterday between whites and blacks, growing out of a fight between a negro boy and a white boy, that was taken up later by older heads that should have been cooler.
Late at night unknown parties visited the still quarter and fired into the negro shanties, fortunately killing no one.
It is said warrants have been issued for some of the leaders.
